title: Partner listing — retention & metrics slate
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working slate for partner listing retention goals plus the minimal metrics and tagging we need to ship and monitor a listing in public cloud marketplaces (AWS/GCP/Azure). The doc combines:
- acceptance checklist for publishing and post-publish health gates
- suggested UX/marketing copy snippets (headline, short blurb, feature bullets, 1-liner) we can iterate with partners
- a pragmatic metric set (impressions -> conversion -> retention) and event list for instrumentation
- risks, mitigations, and a proposed reporting cadence

Audience:
GTM owners, partner engineers, product managers, biz dev, marketplace ops, and the partner success manager owning onboarding.

1) Minimum acceptance checklist (pre-publish) — must be green before we request listing publication:
- Listing metadata complete: product name, short description (<=140 chars), long description (<=4,000 chars), category/tags selected.
- Hero assets: 1 hero tile (1024x576), 3 supporting images/screenshots, 1 logo (512x512) in PNG and SVG.
- Buyer-facing docs linked: pricing sheet PDF, data-retention FAQ, security/architecture diagram.
- Legal/financial: Marketplace contract attached, SKU mapping documented, Billing contact assigned.
- Security & compliance: SOC2 attestation link or summary, encryption/KMS note, data residency note (if applicable).
- Test flow: end-to-end purchase or free-trial provisioning tested in the partner sandbox and recorded (screencap).
- Integration: IAM/service account pattern completed (example policy), sample deployment template (ARM/Terraform/CloudFormation) added to repo.
- Observability: Segment/GTM/GA events defined (see instrumentation below) and routed to analytics workspace; basic dashboards stubbed in Looker/Grafana.
- Release plan: rollout window, owner list, rollback criteria, and support rotation for first 14 days.

2) Post-publish operational gates (first 14 days):
- Impression rate sanity check: impressions >= expected baseline for cohort (baseline = partner pre-launch comms reach estimate). If impressions < 50% of baseline at day 3, pause paid campaigns and investigate listing metadata/visibility.
- Conversion to activation: activation rate >= 4% (install/start trial) at day 7 for self-serve SKUs; if < 2% investigate CTA copy, provisioning latency, and pricing mismatch.
- Provisioning SLA: successful provisioning within target time (<= 10 minutes for self-serve, <= 4 hours for assisted). Error rate <= 2%.
- Refund/rollback rate: refunds or cancellation requests <= 1% of activations in first 14 days.
- Retention cohort 7-day: >= 35% of activations return/use within 7 days. If < 20% set focused UX & product follow-up.

3) Copy snippets — short, flexible, partner-friendly (use as starting point):
- 1-line value prop (for hero):
  "Low-latency, production-grade LLM inference with predictable cost and enterprise controls."
- 140-char short description:
  "Ship LLM features faster with predictable latency, autoscaling GPU pools, and built-in auditing for enterprise workloads."
- 2-3 feature bullets (for listing bullets):
  "• Dedicated & shared hosting modes for predictable throughput and budgets
   • Autoscaling pools + burst capacity to handle traffic spikes
   • Built-in audit logs, KMS integration, and VPC-friendly private deployments"
- CTA variations to A/B test (primary):
  "Start free trial" | "Request a demo" | "Get dedicated capacity"
- Troubleshooting microcopy (for FAQ/snippet):
  "Provisioning taking longer than expected? Check that your VPC peering is active and that your quota is not hit. See troubleshooting guide: <link>"

4) Instrumentation & event taxonomy (minimum events to send to analytics):
- listing.impression (metadata: marketplace, listing_id, traffic_source)
- listing.click_cta (cta_type, listing_id, partner_id)
- trial.provision_start (listing_id, user_id, request_id, region)
- trial.provision_success (request_id, duration_ms, compute_shape)
- trial.provision_failure (request_id, error_code, error_message)
- billing.charge_attempt (request_id, sku, amount, currency, success_bool)
- user.first_active (user_id, listing_id, activation_timestamp)
- user.return (user_id, listing_id, days_since_activation)
Note: tag all events with partner_id and campaign_id where applicable. We recommend wiring these events into Segment and then to BigQuery/Looker for dashboards.

5) Key metrics & definitions (keep these flat and consistent across partners):
- Impressions: unique marketplace views per listing_id per day.
- Click-through rate (CTR): listing.click_cta / listing.impression.
- Activation rate: trial.provision_success / listing.click_cta (for self-serve flows).
- Provisioning latency P50/P90: distribution of trial.provision_success.duration_ms.
- 7-day retention: percent of users who triggered user.return within 7 days.
- 30-day pay conversion: percent of trial.provision_success that converted to paid sku within 30 days.
- LTV (coarse): avg revenue per paying customer projected over 12 months (initial estimate: ARPA * gross margin * retention curve).
- CAC on listing: (total marketplace-channel marketing spend) / (number of paying customers attributed to listing in period).

6) Reporting cadence & dashboards (what to publish & when):
- Daily: impressions, CTR, activations, provisioning error rate. Ops channel alerting for provisioning_error_rate > 2% sustained > 1 hour.
- Weekly: activation funnels, 7-day retention cohort, top failure reasons, SKU usage distribution.
- Monthly: pay conversion, CAC, LTV estimate, campaign attribution breakdown.
- Stakeholders: send weekly digest to partner owner, product PM, marketplace ops, and partner success.

7) Retention experiments ideas (quick hypothesis bank):
- New-user quickstart: add a 60-second guided runbook in-console for first 5 minutes of usage. Hypothesis: reduces time-to-value and improves 7-day retention by 8–12%.
- Onboarding email drip tied to activation event: 3-step series highlighting quick wins and docs. Hypothesis: +5% 30-day conversion.
- Default sample prompts and templates: pre-load 3 domain-specific templates in the sandbox. Hypothesis: +10% trial engagement.

8) Risk & mitigation matrix (top risks for listing lifecycle):
- Low visibility: cause = poor metadata or category mismatch. Mitigation = SEO-copy refresh, re-tagging, coordinate with marketplace contact.
- Provisioning failures: cause = quota, IAM, network. Mitigation = run sandbox stress tests, better error reporting, tightened runbook for SREs.
- Unexpected billing disputes: cause = SKU mismatch or unclear pricing. Mitigation = attach clear pricing sheet, hold post-purchase workflows until billing contact verified.
- Security concerns flagged by marketplace: cause = missing documentation (SOC2, encryption). Mitigation = provide summary page and contact for compliance.

9) Rollout & rollback decision guide:
- Roll forward if: activation rate within expected band and provisioning errors < 2% and 7-day retention > lower-bound threshold.
- Pause/rollback if: provisioning_error_rate > 5% for > 30 minutes OR refunds/cancellations > 3% of activations in first 48 hours.
- Emergency rollback steps: disable listing via partner account (owner: partner-ops@redwood.ai), turn off paid campaigns, spin up incident bridge and notify partners and SRE.

10) Next steps & ownership (first iteration):
- PM (Priya Shah): finalize short description and select initial CTA variant by EOD +3 business days.
- Partner Eng (Ethan Coleman): finish provisioning templates and confirm sandbox test results by EOD +5 days.
- Analytics (Maya Chen): implement event spec in Segment and verify event flow to BigQuery by EOD +7 days.
- Marketplace ops (Diego Alvarez): schedule listing publication window and share marketplace contact info.

Notes and references:
- Use existing style guide for copy (confluence link in linked_artifacts). Keep technical claims conservative and quantifiable.
- Keep hero copy vendor-neutral and developer-first — focus on reliability, cost predictability, and deployment flexibility.

Open questions / decisions to make in follow-ups:
- Decide canonical 7-day retention threshold per vertical (SaaS/ISV vs. internal infra).
- Confirm which events are forwarded to marketplace analytics vs kept internal (privacy concerns).
- Agree on attribution window for CAC (7-day vs 30-day).

Draft change log:
- 2024-11-02: initial draft created (Priya Shah).
- 2024-11-15: added instrumentation event list and acceptance checklist (Ethan Coleman).
- 2024-12-05: updated post-publish gates and rollout guidance after partner sandbox dry run (Maya Chen).

End of document.
